headline: OSISKO GREENLIGHTS C$1.2B CARIBOO UNDERGROUND — 1.89M OZ OVER 10 YEARS, FIRST POUR 2029; TRAFIGURA ANCHORS
snippet: Osisko Gold Group's board approved formal construction of the 100%-owned Cariboo Gold Project in central British Columbia on September 14, committing C$1.2 billion (US$841 million) in capital with Trafigura providing a US$30 million equity anchor and a potential US$120 million gold prepayment facility. The underground mine is now 22% complete, targeting a first gold pour in early 2029 and commercial production in H2 2029, with the 2025 feasibility study projecting 1.89 million ounces over a 10-year mine life.

headline: RECORD GOLD GRADES AT HORSE HEAVEN — RESOLUTION MINERALS HITS 14.8 G/T AU IN 600M IDAHO ZONE
snippet: Resolution Minerals (ASX: RML) released new assay results September 15 from its Golden Gate South prospect within the Horse Heaven Antimony-Tungsten-Gold-Silver Project in Idaho — the project's highest gold grades to date — including 1.0 metre at 14.8 g/t Au, broader zones of 10.2 metres at 1.83 g/t Au and 7.2 metres at 2.35 g/t Au, all from near surface. The results further define an approximately 600-metre-wide gold mineralised zone from the company's 42-hole, 12,236-metre 2026 drill campaign at Golden Gate.

headline: $175M TUNGSTEN REVIVAL: ELMET, BLUE MOON + EQ RESOURCES STRIKE DEAL TO RESTART SPRINGER COMPLEX IN NEVADA
snippet: Blue Moon Metals (TSXV/NASDAQ: BMM), The Elmet Group (NASDAQ: ELMT), and EQ Resources (ASX: EQR) announced September 14 a binding agreement for Elmet to invest US$150 million plus a US$50 million prepayment facility to revive Blue Moon's Springer Tungsten Complex in Imlay, Nevada — historically one of the largest U.S. tungsten mines — with a new Ammonium Paratungstate joint venture. Elmet has secured US$450 million in U.S. government backing and a DLA contract potentially worth US$2 billion; the mine and mill target a Q4 2027 restart with the APT plant restarting H2 2028.

headline: COPPER SLIDES TO 3-WEEK LOW AT $14,065/T — LME INVENTORIES CLIMB AS DOLLAR FIRMS INTO FOMC
snippet: Benchmark LME three-month copper fell 1.2% to US$14,065 per metric tonne on September 14 — a three-week low — as London Metal Exchange inventory levels climbed, easing the supply tightness that drove copper to an all-time record of US$14,875 the prior week. A firming U.S. dollar ahead of Wednesday's FOMC rate decision compounded the pressure; nickel also slid 0.5% to US$16,380 per tonne, its lowest level in two months.

headline: VOX ROYALTY BAGS THREE AUSTRALIAN ROYALTIES FOR A$8.4M — GOLD, COPPER, AND PLATINUM GROUP METALS
snippet: Vox Royalty (TSX/NASDAQ: VOXR) completed three Australian royalty acquisitions on September 14 for A$8.4 million, adding the White Dam Gold Royalty in South Australia, the Kalman Copper Royalty in Queensland, and the Sylvania royalty in Western Australia to its streaming and royalty portfolio. The diversified deal expands Vox's Australasian footprint across gold, copper, and platinum group metals.

headline: ROYAL ROAD DRILLS INTO COLOMBIA GOLD-COPPER-SILVER — GÜÍNTAR FOLLOWS UP 131M AT 1 G/T AuEq IN ANTIOQUIA
snippet: Royal Road Minerals (TSX-V: RYR) commenced diamond drilling at Güíntar on September 14 — the most advanced target within its GAM gold-copper-silver project in Antioquia, Colombia — following up hole GUI-DD-013 which returned 131 metres at 1 g/t gold equivalent including 57 metres at 1.4 g/t Au, 10.2 g/t Ag, and 0.6% Cu. The company also reported 36 metres of continuous rock-chip samples at Algodona averaging 2.14 g/t Au and 6.95 g/t Ag as it advances the GAM portfolio toward a maiden mineral resource.

headline: TALISKER POSTS 4,884 OZ AT 7.99 G/T AU THROUGH AUGUST — PHASE 3 BRALORNE UNDERGROUND LAUNCHED
snippet: Talisker Resources (TSX: TSK) reported its 2026 year-to-date operational results through August 31, showing 4,884 ounces of gold produced from 19,014 tonnes mined at an average grade of 7.99 g/t Au at its Bralorne mine in central British Columbia. Phase 3 underground capital development commenced September 3 — targeting the Bralorne West Zone and new ore headings on the 1060 Level — with the next marine concentrate shipment expected in late October or early November.

headline: NUCLEAR FUEL MARKET 2026: SMR BOOM AND HALEU DEMAND SET TO DOUBLE REACTOR REQUIREMENTS BY 2040
snippet: A September 14 Nuclear Fuel Market 2026 report projects uranium demand to grow approximately 3% annually through 2035, driven by energy security mandates, decarbonization targets, and rapid Small Modular Reactor expansion — with the WNA forecasting reactor requirements to more than double by 2040 as AI data centre operators including Microsoft commit to nuclear power. Supply remains structurally constrained: Kazatomprom has guided 2026 production to approximately 77 million pounds while Cameco faces pipeline challenges at its Saskatchewan operations.

headline: SPROTT URANIUM: SPOT SURGES TO $82 AS MINERS RALLY 17-21% — UTILITIES LOCKING IN SUPPLY AHEAD OF DEFICIT
snippet: Sprott's September 2026 uranium market report documents spot U3O8 rebounding to US$82 per pound (up 8.05%) as utility buyers accelerated term-contract commitments to lock in supply ahead of a projected structural deficit. The Northshore Global Uranium Mining Index rose 17.01% in September while the junior uranium index surged 21.75%, with supply risks deepening as Cameco cut McArthur River guidance and Kazatomprom set 2026 production well below 100% capacity.

headline: GOLDSEEK: AFTER THE INFLATION SHOCK, WHERE MINERS FIND SUPPORT — BUY ZONES AND SIGNALS FOR SEPTEMBER
snippet: GoldSeek's September 13 analysis maps the key technical support and buy zones for gold mining equities following August's CPI-driven selloff, identifying price levels where retail investors may find favourable entry ahead of Wednesday's FOMC decision. The piece argues that above-consensus inflation readings are ultimately bullish for miners when real rates remain below historical tightening peaks — a thesis that gains weight as junior gold miners test their 200-day moving averages ahead of the September 16 rate decision.
